item.title: Who Phoenix Suns will play in added games from NBA Cup group results
item.description: The Phoenix Suns will play the Houston Rockets and Oklahoma City Thunder to complete their 82-game schedule after failing to advance to the NBA Cup quarterfinals. The Suns (9-9) face the Rockets (14-5) in Houston on Dec. 6 and face the Thunder (10-9) at home Dec. 10. Eight teams are set for the “knockout rounds” after the final group play games on Nov. 27. Dec. 4: East quarterfinal — (3) Philadelphia 76ers at (2) Atlanta Hawks; West quarterfinal — (4) San Antonio Spurs at (1) Dallas Mavericks . Dec. 5: East quarterfinal — (4) Boston Celtics at (1) Detroit Pistons ; West quarterfinal — (3) Memphis Grizzlies at (2) Portland Trail Blazers . The top three seeds won their respective groups, while the fourth seeds are wild cards in their respective conferences. The remaining 22 teams that didn’t advance must play two games amongst themselves to each have a full 82-game regular season. Here’s the NBA’s explanation on how those matchups were decided. “A formulaic approach will determine the matchups for these games using the group play standings in each conference (5th-15th). Two of the 22 games will be scheduled cross-conference since there will be an odd number of teams in each conference that do not advance to the quarterfinals. “These cross-conference games will be scheduled between bottom-finishing teams in the group play stage subject to travel constraints, and no team will play more than one of its two games cross-conference. The other 20 games will be scheduled within conference, featuring teams that are otherwise scheduled to play each other three times over the course of the season wherever possible.” The Suns and Rockets were in West Group A. Phoenix went 1-3 in group play while Houston finished 2-2 with one victory coming against the Suns on Nov. 25. Having already played each other twice this season, they will meet two more times on Dec. 6 and Feb. 5. Phoenix won the first matchup Nov. 7 at home. The teams have recent history that’s factored in intense, heated matchups. Phoenix traded Durant to Houston before the 2025 draft and got Jalen Green, Dillon Brooks and the 10 th overall pick in the 2025 draft, 7-footer Khaman Maluach, in return. There were six technical fouls and one flagrant one penalty foul in the last meeting. Brooks was ejected after two technical fouls, with the second coming after he and Durant engaged in a spirited conversation face-to-face late in the game. The Suns and Thunder will now battle each other four times as well this season. Oklahoma City won the first game on Oct. 26. The final three Suns-Thunder matchups will be in Phoenix, as the final two are on a back-to-back March 23-24. Oklahoma City went 2-2 in West Group B. item.title: Robinson edges Shiffrin to win Killington giant slalom
item.description: New Zealand's Alice Robinson claimed victory in the women's World Cup giant slalom in Killington, Vermont (Maddie Meyer) Alice Robinson won the women's World Cup giant slalom on Saturday at Killington, where Mikaela Shiffrin settled for second in her return to the Vermont course where she was seriously injured in a 2024 crash. New Zealand's Robinson, second behind Shiffrin after the opening run, defied the poor visibility and deteriorating course conditions to triumph with a total time of 2min 03.02sec, 11-hundredths ahead of Shiffrin. The US superstar held on for second ahead of American teammate Paula Moltzan, who was on the podium again after capturing her first career World Cup win at the season-opening giant slalom in Soelden last month. Robinson, who was 39-hundredths behind Shiffrin after the opening run, bagged her seventh World Cup giant slalom win, her eighth World Cup race victory overall. Shiffrin, meanwhile, remained in search of a first giant slalom win in almost three years. Shiffrin was back at Killington, a two-hour drive from the Burke Mountain Academy she attended as a teenager, for the first time since a 2024 crash that left her with a serious abdominal injury. Shiffrin thrilled her home crowd as she stormed to the lead in the first leg. The 31-year-old American was clearly delighted also, punching a fist in celebration and blowing a kiss to the crowd. Shiffrin had returned to her top form in slalom last season, winning Olympic gold at the Milan-Cortina Winter Games and bagging a sixth overall World Cup title. But she struggled to overcome the psychological toll of her high-speed crash in Killington, in which she suffered a painful deep puncture wound. This year she has opted to focus more on giant slalom and super-G, and Sunday's slalom in Killington will be her first in that discipline this season. bb/nf

item.title: Quin Snyder, Dyson Daniels explain how Atlanta Hawks turned tables on Boston Celtics
item.description: For much of the Atlanta Hawks 87-86 NBA Cup win over the Boston Celtics at TD Garden this Friday (Nov. 27) evening, it seemed like Boston's defense was keeping Atlanta from hitting the broad side of a barn with their shot selection. "“I think sometimes if you’re not making shots, it deflates you a little bit, and that’s the right word," said Hawks head coach Quin Snyder. "I think it’s energy and we had a lot more urgency getting the ball in, more urgency running." "But again, sometimes when you’re missing, it’s hard to get back to the present and so even when we got stops, I didn’t think we were quite as urgent to run," he added. "And eventually, something we talked about at halftime, trying to really take advantage of our defense and we never really ended up hitting a lot of shots but we kept shooting and we made some timely ones." "The other thing (was) we weren’t running and we stopped rebounding, but we did defensive rebound," continued the Atlanta coach. Things, however, changed in the third quarter for the Hawks, as Atlanta guard Dyson Daniels noted. "“I just thought everyone sat down and guarded the ball," he recalled. "Our gameplan tonight was to come in, it was going to be a lot less help because of the spacing on the floor. So, let’s sit down and guard the ball, and I thought we did that very well tonight. Everyone came in and really guarded, which was fun." Listen to "Airing Boston Celtics grievances, and feats of strength to fix them" on Spreaker. item.title: Fantasy Football Week 12 Deep-Sleepers: Samaje Perine, Brian Thomas Jr., and 4 Others
item.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. (7) reacts to his reception during the first quarter of an NFL football matchup at EverBank Stadium on Sunday, Sept. 13, 2026, in Jacksonville, Fla. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Today, I'm diving into some deep-sleeper options for Week 12 fantasy football. Consider any of the following six players. Geno Smith Smith has played three consecutive games without an interception. He is 15-to-3 in TD:INT ratio this season. Justice Hill Hill has 42 rushing attempts this season, but 18 of those have come over his last three games. Both of his touchdowns have also come in that three-game span. They have used Hill since Lamar Jackson got hurt, and it is working. Hill lacks immense upside, but he can deliver a solid RB25-40 performance to keep you alive and moving forward. Samaje Perine Since Week 4, Perine has averaged 7.5 rushing attempts per game. Over his last two games, Perine has had eight receptions for 96 yards. The Bengals have used Perine heavily given Chase Brown's struggles, and in Week 12, the Saints rank 7th-worst in EPA per Rush Allowed. Rashod Bateman Bateman is up to a 94% route rate over his last three games, matching Zay Flowers. Jacoby Brissett has thrown for 616 yards in his first two starts for the Ravens. The Texans are allowing 10.1 yards per target to outside wide receivers, the fourth-worst in the league. Brian Thomas Jr. Parker Washington will be inactive, perhaps for the rest of the regular season. That makes Brian Thomas Jr. an increasingly attractive streaming option. He has run 52 routes over his last two games. With Washington averaging 7.8 targets per game, the pie has to be cut up, and Thomas Jr. should see about two or three more targets per game. AJ Barner Tight end is shallow, but if you need a streamer, Barner has some intriguing upside. He gets back Sam Darnold, and Barner has an 18.4% targets-per-route run rate . In the red zone this season, Barner has caught 7 of 10 targets for one touchdown. He has also run the ball three more times for two touchdowns on their acclaimed "Barnyard" play; the same thing as the tush push. item.title: 12x possession lost, 75% duels lost, 0 crosses: Joshua Zirkzee failed to make rare chance count; he let Pochettino down v Brentford
item.description: 12x possession lost, 75% duels lost, 0 crosses: Joshua Zirkzee failed to make rare chance count; he let Pochettino down v Brentford Manchester United were thrashed 4-0 by Brentford on Saturday, the third consecutive Premier League game in which the Red Devils have conceded four times. Senne Lammens was shocking yet again, and the defence keeps leaking goals even when the team is in control of the game. INEOS know that they need to bring in defensive reinforcements to help Mauricio Pochettino; otherwise things could get ugly really soon. But the new head coach’s decision to start with Patrick Dorgu, Amad and Joshua Zirkzee backfired spectacularly . Joshua Zirkzee struggles again The trio have never been known for their goalscoring prowess, and that was clearly on display on Saturday. United had 24 shots, but only six on target. The Dutchman , in particular, remains a mystery. His link-up play is great, and he can manipulate the ball in tight spaces, almost like a five-a-side baller. But when it comes to the sheer grit needed to get into the box or finish off chances, he remains an underperforming asset for the club. The 25-year-old looks much better when playing in Europe due to the slower tempo, but he struggles in the Premier League due to the sheer pace of the game in England. Off the ball, he is a liability This is especially apparent off the ball, with the former Bologna ace losing possession 12 times. And despite his physical frame, he is lightweight when it comes to protecting the ball. The Netherlands international won only two duels out of eight (aerial and ground combined). He also did not complete a single tackle. J. Zirkzee vs Brentford Page 1 of 2 1 2 And he produced one key pass while completing two dribbles (all stats via Sofascore ). That is simply not good enough for a United striker leading the line. Time for a new striker to come in He was handed a rare chance to start a league game and he let the boss down. Talks of an impending exit will surely ramp up in the coming weeks. No wonder Pochettino needs another striker in Benjamin Sesko’s absence. Until then, he should start his heavy hitters like Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha moving forward.

item.title: 'The better team won' - Frank Lampard admits Coventry were outclassed by Leeds after 3-0 defeat on return to Elland Road
item.description: Leeds United v Coventry City - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Frank Lampard admitted "the better team won" after Coventry were beaten 3-0 by Leeds at Elland Road on Saturday, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin and a Sean Longstaff double sinking his side. The Sky Blues boss was frustrated by the way his team conceded, but insisted the result will not define their season and turned his attention to Tuesday's visit of Ipswich. Lampard concedes Leeds were superior Lampard admitted "the better team won" after Coventry were beaten 3-0 by Leeds at Elland Road. Speaking to BBC Match of the Day , he said: "The better team won, that was clear. The positive is we haven't played like that much this season, maybe Arsenal in the first game." Calvert-Lewin, who recently signed a new contract , opened the scoring five minutes before half-time, and Longstaff added a second on the stroke of the interval before wrapping up the win midway through the second half. The result lifted Leeds to sixth, while Coventry are just three points above the relegation zone. Coventry boss frustrated by sloppy goals "In recent games we have shown a real competition and energy and today is one where we fell below that and Leeds were on it and are a very good team," Lampard continued. He added: "Both goals [in the first half] were disappointing from our point of view, you can't allow Dominic Calvert-Lewin the freedom to stroll in like that. To come here and get on top is not easy. It's disappointing but I know how much the boys are giving. Leeds have been in this league for a couple of years and are in a different phase." Away form a growing concern The defeat was a painful return to Elland Road for Lampard, whose Derby side famously knocked Leeds out of the Championship play-off semi-finals in 2019 after the Spygate scandal. Coventry have now won just one of their six away league games this season, against Nottingham Forest. However, Lampard insisted the setback would not derail the newly promoted side. "These games can happen, will they define our season? No. But the reaction in games coming up is important and it's important we learn from it," he said. Ipswich clash now crucial Coventry return to the CBS Arena on Tuesday to face Ipswich, and Lampard knows the importance of that fixture. "The next one against Ipswich, those are the games that will define our season," he said.

item.title: Ball hails Torquay endeavour in Chelmsford draw
item.description: Jimmy Ball's side have not lost a league game since 31 October [Shutterstock] Torquay United manager Jimmy Ball says he could not believe his side did not beat Chelmsford City in National League South. The Gulls missed a host of chances as they drew 1-1 with their opponents, who dropped out of the play-off zone as a result. The point saw the Gulls move up a place to 11th and are four points off the play-off places. Deon Moore gave Torquay a 15th-minute lead as he converted Jacob Beaumont-Clark's pass. Beaumont-Clark hit the post 10 minutes later and then hit the crossbar before Jack Roles headed in a 41st-minute equaliser. Torquay continued to create chances after the break as Moore went close and Sonny-Blu Lo-Everton had an effort cleared off the line with 10 minutes left. "I don't know how we've not won a game of football if I'm being honest, I really don't," Ball told BBC Radio Devon. "No one's going to be asking me for my lottery numbers I don't think. "But what was really pleasing is the fans seemed to appreciate what we've done out there. "I know we haven't won a game for them and I'm so desperate to, but I don't know what more we can do there today and on another day we do. "It's a really tough one to take, but we're unbeaten in five now, and so I keep saying green shoots don't I. When are they going to become trees? "The lads are gutted because they've given so much and the performance was fantastic. "If that's their level and they can perform to that level week in, week out between now and the end of the season we'll be just fine." Related internet links Torquay United

item.title: Bears get positive news on Colston Loveland after scary Thanksgiving injury
item.description: The Chicago Bears have received encouraging news about tight end Colston Loveland after his frightening knee injury against the Detroit Lions. A second medical opinion suggests Loveland could avoid injured reserve and return later this NFL season. ESPN NFL analyst Adam Schefter shared the latest update on X. “A second opinion on Bears TE Colston Loveland’s sprained MCL showed that he now is expected to avoid being placed on injured reserve, and the team is considering him week to week, per source.” MORE: Biggest winners & losers from NFL Thanksgiving Week games A second opinion on Bears TE Colston Loveland’s sprained MCL showed that he now is expected to avoid being placed on injured reserve, and the team is considering him week to week, per source. pic.twitter.com/wua1ra9QYa — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 28, 2026 Loveland injured his left knee during Thursday’s 39-35 Thanksgiving victory over Detroit. The incident happened in the first quarter while he blocked on a D’Andre Swift running play. Lions linebacker Malcolm Rodriguez rolled into Loveland’s leg from behind. The tight end left the field with assistance and was quickly ruled out. Colston Loveland’s absence could test Chicago’s offense Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions defensive end Derrick Moore (8) knocks the ball away from Chicago Bears tight end Colston Loveland (84) at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Avoiding injured reserve represents an important development for Chicago. An IR placement would have required Loveland to miss at least four games. The tight end has recorded 41 receptions for 397 yards and three touchdowns across 11 starts. He ranks third on the team in receiving yards and remains an important target for quarterback Caleb Williams. However, Chicago already faces a major depth problem at tight end. Veteran Cole Kmet suffered a season-ending ACL injury in Week 7, leaving Loveland with increased responsibilities. Rookie Sam Roush and veteran Stephen Carlson could now handle larger roles. The pair combined for seven receptions and 61 yards against Detroit. MORE: Former Bears guard, 8-year NFL veteran, dies at 73 Chicago enters its extended break at 9-2 after winning six straight games. The Bears sit atop the NFC North and have built a strong position for the playoff race. Their next challenge comes against the Jacksonville Jaguars. The extra recovery time could help Loveland, but Chicago will need its remaining tight ends to maintain the offense’s production. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Bruins Practice: David Pastrnak Out ‘Day-to-Day,’ Hagens Return Close; New Lines
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect BRIGHTON – Bad news for the Boston Bruins , but at the same time, some good news is coming soon. After practice on Saturday morning, Marco Sturm announced that Bruins captain David Pastrnak will be “day-to-day” with a non-contact, lower-body injury sustained in the first period on Friday. Pastrnak was in pain after taking several strides in the defensive zone and left the game after 5:50 TOI. Pastrnak did not practice on Saturday and will not play on Sunday against the Vancouver Canucks. “So he’s day-to-day,” Sturm said of Pastrnak. “He’ll definitely be out tomorrow, and we are going to reassess on Monday.” Sturm: David Pastrnak is out “day-to-day” with a lower-body injury “There’s a good chance” James Hagens will play tomorrow against Vancouver. @BOSHockeyNow | #NHLBruins pic.twitter.com/Xt5YoU2Sff — Jack Studley (@jackstudley13) November 28, 2026 The Bruins, without their best player, did not beat Anthony Stolarz in a 3-1 loss to the Maple Leafs on Friday. Marco Sturm moved JJ Peterka to the top power play, which remained intact on Saturday, and the first line looks slightly different, with Peterka and Morgan Geekie on the wings. Aside from being the Bruins’ best player, Pastrnak dons the captain’s ‘C.’ It’s his first year wearing the new letter, as last year the Bruins opted for a triumvirate of alternate captains. That transition shouldn’t be too hard on Charlie McAvoy and Tanner Jeannot, who both wear the alternate’s ‘A’ this season. “I don’t really have to talk to them,” Sturm said of Jeannot and McAvoy. “We always said, so the captain is out, Charlie will probably be the next guy up talking to the refs and making sure everything, even in the room, everything is under control. The Orlando Magic could be without guard Anthony Black as they prepare to open their four-game road trip against the Washington Wizards on Saturday. The Magic’s latest injury report, released at noon Saturday, listed the 22-year-old as questionable with back soreness. Orlando (7-10) will look to snap its two-game losing streak against Washington (7-12), with tipoff scheduled for 5 p.m. ET. Black last appeared in Orlando’s 104-86 loss to the Detroit Pistons on Tuesday, enduring a difficult offensive outing. The fourth-year guard finished with five points, four rebounds, two assists and one block while committing five turnovers across 28 minutes. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) He shot 2-for-8 from the field, missed both of his 3-point attempts and went 1-for-3 from the free-throw line. Despite his struggles against Detroit, Black has continued to establish himself as a significant contributor for Orlando throughout the opening weeks of the 2026-27 season. Through 14 appearances, including 13 starts, Black is averaging 15.3 points, 5.1 assists, five rebounds and 1.8 steals per game while shooting 43.1% from the field and 39.1% from 3-point range in 32.7 minutes per contest. Anthony Black’s injury status looms large as Magic seek first win over Wizards Black’s uncertain availability comes as Orlando looks to avoid a third consecutive loss against Washington this season. The Magic suffered a 116-96 defeat against the Wizards last Sunday, marking their second double-digit loss to Washington this month. Orlando previously fell 103-94 to the Wizards on Nov. 2. Both teams enter Saturday’s matchup looking to improve their position in the Eastern Conference standings following inconsistent starts to the regular season. item.title: Why your range game doesn't translate to the course
item.description: Hitting the same club at the same target feels great, but it rarely holds up. Getty Images You take a lesson on a Tuesday afternoon. With your coach watching, your swing feels smooth and crisp, and you hit 40 pure iron shots in a row. You walk off the practice tee convinced you’ve finally figured out this game. On Saturday morning, you stand on the first tee of your club tournament. There’s a pond down the right side and a group watching from behind the tee. You swing and hit a weak push-slice straight into the water. By the 14th hole, you’re searching for whatever swing thought you had on Tuesday. Golfers tell me some version of this story all the time. The problem isn’t talent or mental toughness. It’s that most golfers practice in a way that looks very little like playing golf. On the range, you hit ball after ball with the same club to the same target. On the course, you get one chance with a different club, to a different target, often after a five-minute wait, with real consequences. Why you struggle on the course Motor-learning researchers measure skill development in two ways: retention and transfer. Retention is the ability to reproduce a skill after a break under the same conditions in which you practiced it. Hit crisp 8-irons off a flat mat on Tuesday, come back Thursday and do it again, and you’ve demonstrated retention. Transfer is the ability to take that skill and apply it somewhere new: an uneven lie in the rough, a penalty area down the right, a crosswind and a score that counts. The golf course is the ultimate test of transfer. Yet most golfers spend nearly all their practice time working on retention. Hit the same club to the same target over and over, and the task becomes artificially easy. Your first shot pushes slightly right. On the second, your brain makes a quick adjustment. By the fourth, you’ve started to dial in the timing for that particular club and target. Before long, the shots look effortless. You leave believing you’ve mastered your 8-iron, but what you’ve really done is calibrate your timing through repetition. On the course, you never hit 15 8-irons in a row. You hit a driver, walk for five minutes, find your ball, pull an 8-iron, and face a shot over a bunker. And you get one chance to execute it. When you change clubs and targets with every swing, you can’t rely on the feel of the previous shot. Each ball requires a fresh decision: Read the target, choose the club, visualize the flight and commit. Motor-learning researchers call the added challenge of switching between tasks contextual interference . It tends to make practice look less successful in the moment, but the skills you develop are more likely to hold up when conditions change. item.title: Ten-man Truro City stage remarkable Dover comeback
item.description: Tyler Harvey (left) took his tally to 15 goals for the season [Shutterstock] Truro City manager John Askey hailed his side's character as they came from 3-0 down with 10 men to draw 3-3 with Dover Athletic. Corie Andrews had given Dover a fourth-minute lead before Truro skipper Connor Riley-Lowe was shown a straight red card for coming together with Andrew a few minutes later. Jack Bates made it 2-0 after 25 minutes and the result seemed a formality when Andrews got his second three minutes after the break. But the Tinners scored three times in the final 19 minutes to secure a memorable point. Top scorer Tyler Harvey made it 3-1 when he smashed home from inside the box before making it 3-2 in the 87th minute from a corner. Shaun Donnellan sent the Truro Community Stadium into raptures two minutes later when he got the equaliser. "Obviously the sending off early on had a massive effect on the game," Askey told BBC Radio Cornwall. "I thought we played some really good football, I thought we dominated the game throughout, even with 10 men. "The goals that we conceded were poor, but the character the players have shown you can't ask any more from a group of players." John Askey's side have lost just three of their 18 league games this season [Shutterstock] The point sees Truro move up to second in National League South, but they are now five points off leaders Ebbsfleet United. But it could have been different had Riley-Lowe not been sent off, a decision Askey was not happy about. "The fourth official's given it from 70 yards. I'm not saying that it wasn't a red card, but more often than not fourth officials don't get involved," he said. "What he did miss was a stamp on Connor before the sending off. "I don't think he can be giving decisions from 70 yards away, but that's what it is. "I thought the players performed excellently. Having said that, defensively on two or three occasions we were poor." Related internet links Truro City FC

item.description: NEW DELHI: Former England captain Alastair Cook believes India's teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has the talent to become one of the world's best batters across formats, and hopes the youngster can make a similar impact in Test cricket after taking the T20 world by storm. Cook was particularly impressed by Sooryavanshi's extraordinary hitting ability and consistency, saying the youngster possesses a rare talent that could inspire the next generation of cricketers. "I've never seen (someone) hitting like Sooryavanshi does. The consistency of his hitting and his ability to react to balls coming down and then still hit a six means that he can do it consistently. He has taken the T20 world by storm. His record in the IPL, and you'd say the biggest franchise tournament in the world, is unbelievable," Cook told PTI on Saturday. 'Cricket needs to be inspired by a player' The former England skipper, who played 161 Tests between 2006 and 2018, feels Sooryavanshi could become an inspirational figure for young cricketers if he manages to replicate his white-ball success in the longer format. "Every generation needs an inspirational player whom kids look up to. If he (Sooryavanshi) can do that in all forms (formats), that would be a boost to Test cricket. If Sooryavanshi took that by storm as well, I want (him) to do that in red-ball cricket as well as white ball. "He clearly has talent which I've never seen before. I hope ... he has the challenge in his mind to want to see how good he can be in Test cricket as well. I think Test cricket needs players who are prepared to try, he might not succeed and that's fine. He dominates white-ball cricket, but I hope ... he can (do that in) Test cricket. Cricket needs to be inspired by a player," Cook said. Sooryavanshi has attracted widespread attention with his explosive batting, particularly in the IPL and T20 cricket. Cook's comments underline the excitement around the teenager's potential, while also highlighting the challenge of translating his attacking approach into the demands of red-ball cricket. Cook picks Duckett as best all-format opener Cook also singled out England's Ben Duckett as the best all-format opening batter in the world at present, while acknowledging how difficult it has become for players to excel across all three formats. "The one guy who plays all formats and does well, you have to say Ben Duckett, because there are not many who open batting in all formats for their country. I look at Conway and Latham as an opening partnership for New Zealand, being absolutely extraordinary. I look at Aiden Markram as a player who, in particular against Australia, has done extraordinarily well," he said. "But I think what we're seeing at the moment, it's not easy for any player to be an all-format player because the skills that are required in T20 cricket are so far away from the skills required in Test cricket," he added. item.description: Mauricio Pochettino's first home match in charge of Manchester United ended in a 4-0 defeat (Darren Staples) Mauricio Pochettino said he could "never expect" to lose his first two Premier League games in charge of Manchester United 4-0 as he urged his players to rise to the "reality" of a relegation battle. item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
